prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Make a companion variation of the supplied 1994–95 Jackie Leven illustration, including ONE HAND in the portrait to introduce a more reflective gesture and variety within the website series.

Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and the approved starting point for facial likeness, age, hairstyle, clothing, palette, tonal contrast, brushwork and overall mood. Preserve these carefully.
Image 2 is the ORIGINAL blurry period photograph. It supports the person's identity and suggests a hand-under-chin gesture, but do not reproduce the original room, table, exact pose or other people.

CHANGE:
Jackie is seated with his RIGHT HAND (on the viewer's left) loosely supporting his chin and the side of his jaw. This is a relaxed thoughtful gesture, not a tight fist or a theatrical thinker pose. The base of the curled fingers rests lightly beneath the chin, thumb naturally along the underside of the jaw. The mouth, nose, eyes and characteristic cheeks remain readable and unobscured. Slight natural head inclination toward the hand is acceptable, but preserve the head's proportions, expression and age.
Show the hand fully and enough wrist and forearm to make its connection to the body convincing. The jacketed forearm rises diagonally from the lower viewer-left toward the chin. Elbow and supporting surface can remain outside the image; do NOT add a visible table, chair or prop. Only one hand is visible. Believable adult hand size, exactly five anatomically coherent digits with naturally overlapping curled fingers, correctly connected wrist, no extra digits, no fused fingers, no giant fist. No rings, watch or jewellery.
Pull back the framing just a little if needed to comfortably contain the entire head and the complete hand/wrist/forearm gesture. Keep vertical 4:5 format and ample dark breathing room. The hand should give the lower half of the image an expressive diagonal, while the face stays the main focus. Shoulders and arm dissolve into dark brush traces at the bottom.

INVARIANTS:
Same recognizable Jackie as image 1, mid-forties, same wavy medium-length dark hair, thick brows, eyes, substantial straight nose, natural mouth, fuller cheeks, defined jaw, clean-shaven appearance, dark jacket and open muted-grey shirt. No ageing, no new moustache, no idealization or generic face. Keep the same thoughtful quiet watchfulness; no added smile.
Same restrained matte dry-brush ink style. Render hand and forearm with a FEW broad grey shapes and economical irregular strokes, no photorealistic hand inserted into a drawing, no detailed veins or fingernails. Give the face the same selective simplified treatment as before. Rough broken edges, sparse directional hatching, broad calm light/shadow planes, no slick digital modelling or extra microtexture.
Same subdued NEUTRAL GREY palette on near-black anthracite #0d0f12. No brown, sepia, beige or other colour cast. The hand should be slightly darker than the face, never a big bright patch. Shirt also remains subdued. Dark outer contours merge seamlessly into the page background, no paper frame or border.
No text, signatures, logos, instruments, glasses, props, other people or background scenery. One single portrait.
